text: And I believe the results should be out quite soon.

speaker: Mr Gan Kim Yong
text: So, be patient with us, we are doing the assessment.

speaker: Mr Gan Kim Yong
text: I have to also explain that the assessment differs from country to country.

speaker: Mr Gan Kim Yong
text: While WHO and some countries may have approved the use, we still need to assess the efficacy and safety of this vaccine in our own context.

speaker: Mr Gan Kim Yong
text: So, it will take some time and I believe the results should be out shortly.

speaker: Mr Gan Kim Yong
text: Mr Perera also asked about whether we have learnt the lessons from other countries on the promotion of vaccination.

speaker: Mr Gan Kim Yong
text: Yes, indeed, we watched what the other countries do and we try to learn as much as we can from them, whether it is through promotion, through messaging and even through family members to encourage them.

speaker: Mr Gan Kim Yong
text: I think all of us will understand that every country is different, the culture is different, the context is different and beliefs are different.

speaker: Mr Gan Kim Yong
text: Therefore, we also have to evolve our own system of outreach to encourage people to sign up for vaccination.

speaker: Mr Gan Kim Yong
text: I must say that I am encouraged by the take-up rate so far.

speaker: Mr Gan Kim Yong
text: But I think it is always the last 20% to 25% that is most difficult to reach.

speaker: Mr Gan Kim Yong
text: Therefore, I would encourage all of us, Members of Parliament, as well as grassroots leaders, to do what we can to reach out, especially the harder to reach, the older population, to help to explain to them the importance of vaccination.

speaker: Mr Gan Kim Yong
text: I do house visits myself, before the recent tightening of the measures.

speaker: Mr Gan Kim Yong
text: I bring along my grassroots leaders to see whether we can persuade the individuals, the seniors at home, to sign up and we help them sign up on the spot because many of them are waiting for their children, and their children will be very busy and unable to help them.

speaker: Mr Gan Kim Yong
text: So, we tried our best to reach out to them and make it easy for them to sign up.

speaker: Mr Gan Kim Yong
text: We also organise activities on the ground; to invite the seniors to come down, explain to them why vaccination is important and to also help set up a station to help them sign up on the spot.

speaker: Mr Gan Kim Yong
text: I think there are quite a few things that we can do and we can have our own way of reaching out to the seniors, to see how we can further promote vaccination among them.

speaker: Mr Gan Kim Yong
text: Again, it is also important to stamp out false information, misinformation and rumours that may stop them or discourage them from getting vaccinated.

speaker: Mr Gan Kim Yong
text: So, I would encourage all of us to verify our message that we have received before we virtually just forward them to all our friends.

speaker: Mr Gan Kim Yong
text: If they are not true, please do not forward them.

speaker: Ms Ng Ling Ling (Ang Mo Kio)
text: One clarification is that with the resurgence of the community cases happening just a few months after our Phase Three re-opening from end of December last year, and with the roll-out of vaccination, what is the learning?

speaker: Ms Ng Ling Ling (Ang Mo Kio)
text: And how might we plan our re-opening differently this round, after the current tightening measures, ending May, especially with the June school holidays coming up?

speaker: Ms Ng Ling Ling (Ang Mo Kio)
text: Should we be prepared for the measures to maybe last for a longer period?

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: But really, even if we were to be able to do that, there is no place for complacency in our community.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: We all still need to realise, whatever we do on our borders as you heard just now, even for places that have been very, very tight – China Australia, Taiwan – cases leak through.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: Even in our community, it is not likely that we have ever throughout this whole period been able to eradicate the virus.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: There has always been a low level of circulation.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: So, even if we can get today's outbreak under control and we start resuming more activities, there is no place for complacency.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: We must remain alert, vigilant and uphold all the necessary safe management measures.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: Second, vaccinations, as I have said, is an important game changer.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: Today, you have heard where we are now, we are making good progress.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: By May, June, July, we will continue to scale up and get more of our population vaccinated.

speaker: Mr Pritam Singh (Aljunied)
text: First, a quick response to Minister for Home Affairs on his short statement.

speaker: Mr Pritam Singh (Aljunied)
text: Yesterday, the Head of the Workers' Party media team, Mr Leon Perera, put out this Facebook post, this is 13 hours ago: "It is important that as a society, we each do our part to help make sure that difficult times bring out the best and not the worst in Singapore.

speaker: Mr Pritam Singh (Aljunied)
text: We should take heed of incidents like this as it is a reminder of the part we all play to deny acceptability to acts of hate such as this appears to be." This was in response to the Police announcement that it was investigating a man accused of using a racial slur and kicking a 55-year-old woman.

speaker: Mr Pritam Singh (Aljunied)
text: I have two supplementary questions with regard to the Statement by the Minister for Health.

speaker: Mr Pritam Singh (Aljunied)
text: The first pertains to the HSA safety update that was recently released.

speaker: Mr Pritam Singh (Aljunied)
text: It covered the suspected adverse event reports and I think this is a very important document released by MOH, because there is significant misinformation fuelled by not just misinformation alone, but different understanding of the safety of the vaccine.

speaker: Mr Pritam Singh (Aljunied)
text: So, it is not necessarily misinformation, but genuine concerns that people may have.

speaker: Mr Pritam Singh (Aljunied)
text: The Workers' Party Members of Parliament have been doing their part to encourage older Singaporeans, in particular, to get vaccinated.

speaker: Mr Pritam Singh (Aljunied)
text: My second question is, again, to the Minister for Health.

speaker: Mr Pritam Singh (Aljunied)
text: This pertains to the cluster at Tan Tock Seng Hospital.

speaker: Mr Pritam Singh (Aljunied)
text: We have some residents – as I am sure Members in this House also have – who are in Tan Tock Seng Hospital because of some terminal illness or who are very ill.

speaker: Mr Gan Kim Yong
text: We will try to make our report as easy to understand as possible.

speaker: Mr Gan Kim Yong
text: Maybe we will rely on "Mr Phua Chu Kang" to help us convey some of these messages.

speaker: Mr Gan Kim Yong
text: I believe some of you have seen the recent video that we have put out, which has been very effective in communicating some of these messages.

speaker: Mr Gan Kim Yong
text: We will see how we can make it simpler, easier to understand and to also avoid misunderstandings and rumours.

speaker: Mr Gan Kim Yong
text: We will make adjustments and we will make allowance for them to visit as much as possible, but to also take into account the various precautionary measures that have to be put in place.

speaker: Mr Speaker
text: The Clerk will now proceed to read the Orders of the Day.
